artists.biography: There are at least two artists on last.fm under the name "Whiteout": 1) Whiteout, the band, were from Greenock, Scotland. Their amalgam of country rock influences such as The Byrds and classic rock riffs of bands like Mott the Hoople and The Faces were warmly received by the rock critics in the UK and American press. In 1994 they released the singles "Detroit", "No Time" and "Starrclub" followed by their debut album “Bite It” in 1995 on Silvertone Records (ex-label of The Stone Roses). This was followed by another single "Jackie's Racing". “Detroit” and “Starrclub” did not appear on the album. In 1995 they shared equal billing on Oasis' first UK tour. Their second album, "Big Wow" was self-released in 1998 and was accompanied by a single called "Kickout”. 2) whiteout (aka Dawk Suice aka The PillsBury FlowBoy aka Angel Pagan, The OyxMoron): MC/C.A.E./Promoter (Rich Quick/SiNISTER/Charlie Blaze)/Producer b. July 24, 1984, Minneapolis, MN, USA whiteout won third place in VIBE's "No. 1 Stan" contest: "June 11, 2009 Dear VIBE Reader, Thank you for you participation in the "VIBE Verses Presents No. 1 Stan" contest! Congratulations on being selected as a third place winner! Your Submission was hot and beat out many others to be amongst the finalists. Your work made it a very tough decision for Eminem to select the final two. You weren't chosen as a finalist, but because of all your hard work and creativity, we are sending you a copy of Relapse (Shady/Aftermath/Interscope) signed by Eminem, enclosed in this mailing. perplexity.description:
Bite It is the debut album by Scottish rock band Whiteout, released in 1995 on Silvertone Records, a label known for its association with influential acts like The Stone Roses. The album showcases a blend of melodic rock with a Britpop edge, characterized by catchy hooks, energetic guitar work, and a raw yet polished production style typical of mid-1990s British rock. Notable tracks include the singles "No Time" and "Jackie's Racing," which highlight the band's ability to combine driving rhythms with memorable choruses.

As Whiteout's first full-length release, Bite It established their presence in the UK rock scene during a period dominated by Britpop and alternative rock. While it did not achieve major commercial success, the album received positive attention for its solid songwriting and the band's spirited performance. It remains a significant entry in Whiteout's discography, capturing the band's early sound and potential within the mid-90s rock landscape.
